function.mechanism: Acts as a water-miscible carrier/solvent that dissolves and distributes flavorings and additives; also binds water to reduce drying and maintain texture.

adi.basis: SCF-derived ADI from chronic rat data (NOAEL 2,500 mg/kg bw/day, UF 100); EFSA 2018 concluded no reason to revise.

efsa.key_finding: EFSA re-evaluation retained ADI 25 mg/kg bw/day; refined brand-loyal mean and P95 exposures did not exceed ADI, with highest reported P95 of 23.3 mg/kg bw/day in children.

adi.basis: JECFA ADI listed as 0-25 mg/kg bw (allocated 1973); database entry evaluation year 2002 with flavoring-use evaluation note.

concerns.summary: In mice, 28-day oral dosing at 1 and 5 g/kg/day produced nephrotoxicity markers; this is far above typical food-additive exposure levels.
Human patch-test literature indicates propylene glycol can act as a weak skin allergen in some contexts, mainly relevant to dermal exposure.
A severe toxicity case (metabolic acidosis/multisystem illness) was reported in an adolescent with extreme chronic cornstarch ingestion, representing atypical high exposure.
In vitro co-exposure work suggests propylene glycol may increase dispersion/solubility and cytotoxicity of ZnO nanoparticles, indicating interaction-dependent rather than standalone hazard.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA 2018 found no genotoxicity concern in the evaluated dataset.
EFSA retained ADI at 25 mg/kg bw/day and found refined P95 dietary exposure below ADI.
No IARC Group classification entry identified for propylene glycol in the current IARC list dataset.

adi_exceedance.notes: EFSA refined brand-loyal scenario did not exceed ADI in any population group; highest P95 reported was 23.3 mg/kg bw/day in children.

risk_assessment.rationale: Major regulators maintain approval with an established ADI and EFSA did not identify ADI exceedance in refined exposure scenarios. Evidence of harm is mainly associated with high-dose or atypical exposures rather than routine regulated dietary intake.
key_factors: EFSA retained ADI 25 mg/kg bw/day in 2018
Refined EFSA exposure scenario remained below ADI (highest P95 23.3 mg/kg bw/day in children)
FDA status is GRAS under 21 CFR 184.1666 with cGMP constraints
No current IARC group listing identified for propylene glycol
